# GENERATED DATA. Do not edit by hand: an external generator rewrites this file
# from the fleet model registry, and a hand edit is lost on the next run.
#
# The approved local model for each type of work and each tier of host, read by
# `scripts/ollama_models.sh select <type>` (ai_model_resolve in
# lib/ollama_endpoint.sh). Format, one entry per line, fields split by spaces:
#
#   threshold <key> <whole GiB>
#   type <type> <small> <standard> <large> <xlarge>
#   size <model> <class> <GPU GiB> <memory GiB or ->
#
# A size line (optional; a file without any still works) gives a model's size
# class (the lowest tier it is meant for) and its floor: a measured host runs
# it when its largest GPU has at least <GPU GiB>, or its memory is at least
# <memory GiB> ("-": GPU only; a mixture-of-experts model runs on the CPU).
# A host under the floor gets the next lower tier's model for that type.
# scripts/ollama_tiers_check.sh checks the file.
#
# Every type names a model for all four tiers. A tier with no model of its own
# repeats the one below it, so a reader never has to work out a fallback.
# Blank lines and lines starting with "#" are ignored.
#
# Tier of a host (memory and largest GPU in whole GiB, as the machine reports
# them; each floor sits one below the nominal size: 30 is a 32 GB machine):
#   xlarge    largest GPU >= xlarge_vram_gb
#   large     largest GPU >= large_vram_gb, or memory >= large_ram_gb
#   small     memory and largest GPU both < small_below_ram_gb
#   standard  otherwise, and whenever memory cannot be read
# AI_MODEL_TIER=small|standard|large|xlarge names the tier instead.

threshold small_below_ram_gb 11
threshold large_ram_gb 30
threshold large_vram_gb 11
threshold xlarge_vram_gb 23
